answer: Echo-Path Triangulation. Each agent periodically pings random peers; honest nodes relay only paths that reconverge through distinct neighborhoods, and the union forms a nebula of overlapping routes rather than a single hub. A new identity must be embedded in that atlas of distinct neighborhoods before its messages propagate, forcing attackers to recruit many spatially separate hosts. Non-reconverging identities are quarantined, so each fake node costs genuine hosting on scattered violet subnets, priced per distinct neighborhood.
